title: Deciphering neuroprotective mechanism of nitroxoline in cerebral ischemia: network pharmacology and molecular modeling-based investigations.
authors: Vadak, Namrata; Borkar, Maheshkumar R; Bhatt, Lokesh Kumar
one_liner_zh: 该文用网络药理学和分子对接研究硝羟喹啉抗脑缺血机制，虽涉及蛋白靶点对接，但核心是药物-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Cerebral ischemia is one of the major causes of death and disability worldwide. Currently, existing approved therapies are based on reperfusion and there is an unmet need to search for drugs with neuroprotective effects. The present study aims to investigate the neuroprotective mechanisms of nitroxoline, a nitro derivative of 8-Hydroxyquinoline, against cerebral ischemia using integrated network pharmacology and molecular docking approaches. Critical analytical tools used were SwissTarget, PharmMapper, BindingDB, DisGeNet, Cytoscape, GeneMANIA, ShinyGo, Metascape, GeneCodis, and Schrodinger GLIDE. Thirty-six overlapping drug and disease targets were identified and used for further analysis. Gene Ontology results showed that nitroxoline enriched the genes involved in biological processes of oxidative stress and apoptotic cell death that are highly implicated in hypoxic injury. KEGG enrichment analysis showed nitroxoline influenced a total of 159 biological pathways, out of which, top pathways involved in cerebral ischemia included longevity regulating pathway, VEGF signaling, EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor resistance, IL-17 and HIF-1 pathways, FoxO signaling, and AGE-RAGE pathway. Protein-protein interaction analysis using string database showed PARP1, EGFR, PTEN, BRD4, RAC1, NOS2, MTOR, MAPK3, BCL2, MAPK1, APP, METAP2, MAPK14, SIRT1, PRKAA1, and MCL1 as highly interactive proteins involved in pathogenesis of ischemic stroke regulated by nitroxoline. The highly interactive protein targets were validated by molecular docking studies and molecular dynamic simulations. Amongst all these targets, nitroxoline showed the highest binding affinity towards BRD4 followed by PARP1 and PTEN. Nitroxoline, through network pharmacology analysis, showed a role in regulating proteins, biological processes, and pathways crucial in cerebral ischemia. The current study thus provides a preliminary insight that nitroxoline might be used as a neuroprotectant against cerebral ischemia via modulating the epigenetic reader BRD4 and transcription factors such as RELA, NF-kappabeta1, and SP1. However, further in-vitro and preclinical studies need to be performed for concrete evidence.
abstract_zh: 脑缺血是全球范围内导致死亡和残疾的主要原因之一。目前，已批准的疗法基于再灌注，且存在未满足的需求，即寻找具有神经保护作用的药物。本研究旨在利用整合的网络药理学和分子对接方法，探讨硝基喹啉（nitroxoline，8-羟基喹啉的硝基衍生物）对抗脑缺血的神经保护机制。使用的关键分析工具包括SwissTarget、PharmMapper、BindingDB、DisGeNet、Cytoscape、GeneMANIA、ShinyGo、Metascape、GeneCodis和Schrodinger GLIDE。共识别出36个重叠的药物和疾病靶点，并用于进一步分析。基因本体论结果显示，硝基喹啉富集了涉及氧化应激和凋亡性细胞死亡生物学过程的基因，这些过程与缺氧损伤高度相关。KEGG富集分析显示，硝基喹啉影响了总共159条生物通路，其中与脑缺血相关的主要通路包括长寿调节通路、VEGF信号通路、EGFR酪氨酸激酶抑制剂耐药性、IL-17和HIF-1通路、FoxO信号通路以及AGE-RAGE通路。使用STRING数据库进行的蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用分析显示，PARP1、EGFR、PTEN、BRD4、RAC1、NOS2、MTOR、MAPK3、BCL2、MAPK1、APP、METAP2、MAPK14、SIRT1、PRKAA1和MCL1是受硝基喹啉调控的缺血性卒中发病机制中高度相互作用的蛋白质。这些高度相互作用的蛋白质靶点通过分子对接研究和分子动力学模拟进行了验证。在所有靶点中，硝基喹啉对BRD4表现出最高的结合亲和力，其次是PARP1和PTEN。通过网络药理学分析，硝基喹啉显示出在调控脑缺血关键蛋白质、生物学过程和通路中的作用。因此，本研究提供了初步见解，即硝基喹啉可能通过调节表观遗传阅读器BRD4以及转录因子如RELA、NF-kappabeta1和SP1，作为对抗脑缺血的神经保护剂。然而，仍需进一步的体外和临床前研究以获取确凿证据。
